item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

So, here we have a skip that kills performances in the sense it causes a key actor to undergo an incredible mental decline. If allowed to do its thing on another uncontained broadcast based anomalies, like SCP-1241 before it was neutralized, it is arguable that 878 could stop such broadcasts or allow easier containment. As such, I am proposing the following edits:

Changing this:

To the extent that they are a single entity, SCP-878's motives are unknown. No records of SCP-878-1 appearing in any media without SCP-878-2 exist, and his real identity is unknown.

To this:

To the extent that they are a single entity, SCP-878's motives are unknown. No records of SCP-878-1 appearing in any media without SCP-878-2 exist, and his real identity is unknown. Proposals for controlled use of SCP-878 as a means of containing broadcast based anomalies, such as SCP-1241, upon containment are currently under review.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

" Addendum 878-B: At the request of Foundation historians, investigation is ongoing as to whether [REDACTED] can be explained in part by SCP-878. However, it has been confirmed that the actor [REDACTED] did take part in a performance of "Hamlet" three weeks before the assassination of [REDACTED], playing the role of Rosencrantz. item.content:encoded:
I see a solid core here, but here's what I would change.

Drop the part about culturally signifigant actors. I see that you are trying to show the callousness of the foundation via them just dismissing the victims as irrelevant, and that is a good element. But it makes them seem even more callous if they just disregard all actors as irrelevant. And honestly, I can't think of a single actor who's erasure would seriously effect the world. Maybe John Wilkes Booth.

The "how did the foundation notice this?" question is problematic. You can't leave it unaddressed, and you can't go into too much detail without it seeming contrived. Hmmmmm…maybe change the mechanics of the change to something other than reality-bending. Maybe it just effects media (scripts, recordings, broadcasts, etc.) but leaves memories of viewers unchanged. Or maybe it would be better the other way 'round, with memories altered but documentation remaining fromt the original timeline.

All in all, I'll up-vote it for a good concept.

the butterfly effect i want to address there….i'm a huge proponent of just how severe the butterfly effect IS, how much people ignore it when they do things involving any kind of time travel….

but what i love about this is the idea that the reality shift that happens is shifting to a reality in which despite the differences, the timeline that gets followed is one in which things happened in such a way to be AS CLOSE AS POSSIBLE to the original reality.

if one accepts infinite possibility, then a universe exists in which that is what the past was, and it still turned out into this kind of present, and that's what we got shifted to.

"reality-shift immune personnel" was dumb, retroactive serial killer was a bit iffy but i found it interesting given the view i had on how this works, and i have no answer to your other points. but the nullification of the butterfly effect is the very reason WHY i like this one.

item.content:encoded:
Bland's comment included the phrase "too much handwaving into a diabolus ex machina." I didn't contest it. I tried to keep this as slim as possible, so I waved a lot of stuff away. The SCP Foundation doesn't have experts in American culture who can determine whether one person is worth more culturally than another, but 878 isn't killing Robert Mitchum, so…acceptable losses are acceptable. As for the butterfly effect, the entry does mention that after SCP-878-2's effect, a fundamentally similar script is followed with a fundamentally similar actor; with a waving of the hand, one can presume that life as a larger whole carried on without the rest of the events of the actor's life. Maybe his parents had another kid later and their lives were complete, almost as if nothing had ever happened. And I edited out the immune-personnel thing, though that left a plot hole in the addendum as to how "reports were compiled" exactly.

tl,dr: I was shooting for brevity and let some things slip deliberately, things that are less vital. My last SCP got depth-charged because I went into way, way too much detail about everything (in part), so I just let the reader fill in details.

If you don't like it, I can't quite blame you; it's a matter of taste. SCP-682's entry never explains why hydrochloric acid incapacitates him when almost nothing else does. This obviously isn't that good, but…some things just have to be waved away.

In earilier drafts, I mentioned both a reality-shift detector and checking IMDB, actually. Suggestions here got me to edit the less-plausible details out.
